title: Dickepechegans
summary: Dickepechegans is Tooker's recorded Indigenous placename for the Huntington hills now known as Dix Hills. The modern name is explained through Dick Pechegan, whose home and planted fields were associated with the hills.
address_label: Dix Hills, Town of Huntington, NY
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Dickepechegans, dick-petheyans, dich-pechegans, Pechegin, and Pichegan. The name is treated as a personal name in the possessive case rather than a topographic translation: Dick was attached to the Indigenous name Pechegan.

Why Place Names Matter

“In many Indigenous cultures, place names are descriptive, but not necessarily unique, as is the case with western or European naming.”

— Lynn Peplinski, Place Names (2018), Article paragraph 5

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
land_loss_content: Dickepechegans shows how Indigenous personal names, homes, and planting places remained embedded in Long Island geography even after English forms became dominant. Reconnecting Dix Hills to Dick Pechegan restores an older layer of memory to a familiar modern name.
whereintheworld_content: Tooker associates these hills with modern Dix Hills. The exact locations of Dick Pechegan's wigwam and fields have not been established.
